answer: For 2025 L'Oreal reported 56% progress toward using 100% recycled and reused water for industrial purposes at factories by 2030, and 57% progress on offering water-saving products or technologies in water-stressed markets. Total water consumption was 954,075 cubic metres, including 383,008 cubic metres in areas at water risk; total water recycled and reused was 940,246 cubic metres; and water intensity was 22 cubic metres per million euros of net sales on own operations. The water-risk indicator is calculated on the Group factory scope, which was defined in 2025.

evidence.quote: By 2030, L'Oréal aims to use 100% recycled and reused water for industrial purposes at its factories.
